narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
intent: To illustrate the growth in the proportion of adult internet users posting online video from 2009 to 2013.

units.meaning: In 2009, 14% of adult internet users posted online video.

basis.note: Table row for 2009 gives value=14 and unit=%.

accepted_routes: 14% of adult internet users posted online video in 2009.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The 2009 value 14% must be visible or labeled.
units.temporal_anchor: 2009 clause or start of the 2009-to-2013 span.
units.reviewer_question: Must the 2009 baseline (14%) be explicitly conveyed?

units.meaning: In 2013, 31% of adult internet users posted online video.

basis.note: Table row for 2013 gives value=31 and unit=%.

accepted_routes: 31% of adult internet users posted online video in 2013.
By 2013, the share had reached 31 percent.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The 2013 value 31% must be visible or labeled.
units.temporal_anchor: 2013 clause or end of the 2009-to-2013 span.
units.reviewer_question: Must the 2013 endpoint (31%) be explicitly conveyed?

units.meaning: The proportion posting online video increased from 2009 to 2013; 2013 is higher than 2009.
accepted_routes: The share rose from 14% in 2009 to 31% in 2013.
There was an upward change over the period.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The visual encoding must make clear that the 2013 value exceeds the 2009 value.
units.reviewer_question: Is the upward direction required as a separate unit, or is it implied by the two endpoint values?

units.meaning: The increase from 2009 to 2013 was 17 percentage points (31% minus 14%).
accepted_routes: The gain from 2009 to 2013 was 17 points.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The chart must allow the 31% and 14% values to be compared so that a 17-point difference is derivable or labeled.
units.reviewer_question: Must the absolute percentage-point gain (17 pp) be conveyed, or is the ratio/doubling sufficient?

units.meaning: The 2013 proportion was more than double the 2009 proportion; 31% is about 2.2 times 14%, an increase of about 121% relative to 2009.

basis.note: Base value for ratio and relative change.
Comparison value for ratio and relative change.

accepted_routes: The share more than doubled, from 14% to 31%.
The 2013 share was about 2.2 times the 2009 share.
It increased by roughly 120% relative to 2009.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The chart must show both 14% and 31% so the ratio or more-than-doubling is derivable or explicitly annotated.
units.reviewer_question: Should the video be required to state the growth as more than doubled/about 2.2x, given the narration says 'doubled' but the table shows 31% vs. 14%?

optional_valid: The time span is four years: 2013 - 2009 = 4.
The 2009 value is about 45.16% of the 2013 value: 14 / 31 = 0.4516.
unsupported_to_avoid: Causal claims such as a specific platform or technology causing the growth.
Absolute counts of adult internet users or video posters; the denominator is not in the table.
Values for years other than 2009 and 2013.
Exact 'doubled' as 28% or exact 100% increase; 31 / 14 = 2.21 is more than double.
Continuous annual trend shape or per-year values between the endpoints.
notes: The table gives two absolute percentage values: 14% in 2009 and 31% in 2013. Derived comparisons support 17 percentage points and about 2.2x/more-than-doubled, so avoid importing counts, causality, or exact doubling language.
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
